Fall 2026" format: revealjs: theme: default highlight-style: github incremental: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 3.5 scrollable: true slide-number: true execute: echo: true warning: false cache: true --- # Share! ## [`{datapasta}`](https://github.com/MilesMcBain/datapasta) * Copy and paste data to and from `R` * VERY handy! * Good for [reprex](https://github.com/tidyverse/reprex) + posting questions on [Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co/) or stackoverflow [**demo**]{style="color:#D55E00;"} ## Housekeeping * Sharing a [postdoc opening](https://www.jobbnorge.no/en/available-jobs/job/309569/postdoctoral-fellows-in-educational-measurement) on behalf of a colleague * Homework 1 due today * Groups due today - I need emails from everyone by 5pm (if you have not already emailed) - Anyone have data they want to use? # Homework 1 Review # Data Visualization with {ggplot2} Week 3 ## Agenda {.smaller} `{ggplot2}` * syntax * continuous data visualizations * categorical data visualizations * options + color/fill + transparency + labels + facets **Learning Objectives** * Understand the basic syntax requirements for `{ggplot2}` * Recognize various options for displaying continuous and categorical data * Familiarity with various `{ggplot2}` options + color/fill + transparency + labels + facets ## ![](https://cdn.myportfolio.com/45214904-6a61-4e23-98d6-b140f8654a40/b467ee99-87e3-4663-ae27-aaf027f940ce_rw_1920.png?h=0573cb8b960ba2f2c8486188761f03e0){width="70%"} ::: aside Credit [Allison Horst](https://allisonhorst.com/data-science-art) ::: ## Providing grammar for: {.smaller} * Graphics + `{ggplot2}` * Data manipulations + `{dplyr}` + `{tidyr}` * Expanding area of specialized topics + `{lubridate}` + `{glue}` + `{tidymodels}` * Many more... ## Providing grammar for: {.smaller} * Graphics + `{ggplot2}` * Data manipulations + `{dplyr}` + `{tidyr}` * Expanding area of specialized topics + `{lubridate}` + `{glue}` + `{tidymodels}` * Many more... # {ggplot2} ## The `{ggplot2}` package `gg` stands for the "grammar of graphics" :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](https://ggplot2-book.org/cover.jpg){width="50%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](https://images-us.bookshop.org/ingram/9780387245447.jpg?height=500&v=v2) ::: :::: ## Components {.smaller} Every `ggplot` figure has three components 1. **data** + the `data` used to produce the plot 2. **aesthetic mappings (`aes`)** + between variables and visual properties 3. **layer(s)** + usually through the `geom_*()` function to produce geometric shapes to be rendered . . . **`ggplot()` always takes a data frame (tibble) as the first argument** ## Basic syntax {.smaller} [ggplot(]{style="color:#D55E00"}[data]{style="color:#0072B2"}, [aes(]{style="color:#009E73"}x = xvar, y = yvar[)]{style="color:#009E73"}[)]{style="color:#D55E00"} [+]{style="color:#CC79A7"}
     [geom_function()]{style="color:#E69f00"} . . . [ggplot()]{style="color:#D55E00"} = the function is `ggplot()` and the package is `{ggplot2}` . . . [data]{style="color:#0072B2"} = the data to be plotted . . . [aes(]{style="color:#009E73"}x = xvar, y = yvar[)]{style="color:#009E73"} = the `aes`thetic mappings . . . [geom_function()]{style="color:#E69f00"} = the `geom`etrics of the plot; the "[function()]{style="color:#E69f00"}" here represents any of the `geom_*` offerings . . . ::: {.fragment} note the [+]{style="color:#CC79A7"} and NOT the `|>` ::: ## `{ggplot2}` template ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data, aes(mappings)) + geom_function() ``` ::: . . . or equivalently . . . ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data |> ggplot(aes(mappings)) + geom_function() ``` ::: ## Some data for today ![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png){fig-align="right" width="30%"} [run the following]{style="color:#D55E00;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(palmerpenguins) head(penguins) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 8 species island bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g 1 Adelie Torgersen 39.1 18.7 181 3750 2 Adelie Torgersen 39.5 17.4 186 3800 3 Adelie Torgersen 40.3 18 195 3250 4 Adelie Torgersen NA NA NA NA 5 Adelie Torgersen 36.7 19.3 193 3450 6 Adelie Torgersen 39.3 20.6 190 3650 # ℹ 2 more variables: sex , year ``` ::: ::: # Continuous Data ## Setting up a plot Run the following code. What do you see? ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/pengemp-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Setting up a plot We have to add some layers! ![](./images/owl.PNG) ## Setting up a plot It's ready for you to add some `geom`etric layers...what should we add? ## How about points? ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|3"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Adding layers * In the previous slide, we added a layer of points * The `geom_point()` layer is a function, complete with it's own arguments . . . Let’s change the color of the points How would you change the color of the points? or How would you find out about changing the color of the points? . . . `?geom_point` ## `color` ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|3"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "magenta") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/peng-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Add another layer Let's add a smoothed line with `geom_smooth()` ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|4"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "magenta") + geom_smooth() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Add another layer Let's add a smoothed line with `geom_smooth()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="3"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "magenta") + geom_smooth() ``` ::: *Note*: This is **NOT** the same as `geom_line()`. We are fitting a line of best fit with `geom_smooth()` ## You try You probably got the [message]{style="color:#CC79A7;"} below when you ran (defaults) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "magenta") + geom_smooth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x' ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/peng-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: . . . Change the `method` to `"lm"` ## Let's do this one together Look at the help page – `?geom_smooth` 1. Remove the `confidence` interval around the line 2. Now change the `*SE*` band to reflect a 68% confidence interval ## `color`: global vs. conditional Prior examples changed colors globally - `geom_point(color = "magenta")` . . . Use `aes()` to access variables, and color according to a specific variable . . . - We use variable names within `aes()` . . . Let’s check the data again (`head()`) and the "species" variable (`table()`) . . . [let's do this together]{style="color:#D55E00;"} ## ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|3"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(aes(color = species)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/peng-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## `color`: global vs. conditional ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(aes(color = species)) ``` ::: * When we did `geom_point(color = "magenta")` we put quotes around the color * Why now is "species" not in quotes? . . . * color names/hex codes are in quotes **NOT** in the `aes()` * variable names are in the `aes()` **NOT** in quotes * `aes()` is where you map to your data! ## Conditional flow through layers {.smaller} If we use something like `color = “x”` in the first `aes`thetic, it will carry on through all additional layers These two codes are the same: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(aes(color = species)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> gplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g, color = species)) + geom_point() ``` ::: . . . But these two are not...why? [run to find out]{style="color:#D55E00;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(aes(color = species)) + geom_smooth() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g, color = species)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() ``` ::: ## Be mindful with `aes()` Using `aes()` when you **don't** need it What is happening here? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(aes(color = "blue")) + geom_smooth() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Be mindful with `aes()` **Not** using `aes()` when you need it What is happening here? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = species) + geom_smooth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! object 'species' not found ``` ::: ::: ::: aside Kind of helpful message here. ::: ## Get a little fancy * You can use `geom_point()` for more than one layer * You can also use a different data source on a layer * Use these two properties to highlight points + How about penguins from Torgersen Island? ## ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "black") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="4"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "black") + geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(penguins, island == "Torgersen"), color = "magenta") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="5"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "black") + geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(penguins, island == "Torgersen"), color = "magenta") + geom_smooth(se = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="6"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "black") + geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(penguins, island == "Torgersen"), color = "magenta") + geom_smooth(se = FALSE) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Another option `{gghighlight}` varying flexibility ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|4"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point(color = "magenta") + gghighlight::gghighlight(island == "Torgersen") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Line plots When should you use line plots instead of smooths? . . . * *Usually when time is involved* . . . What are some good candidate data for line plots? . . . * *Oserved versus model-implied (estimated)* ## `geom_line()` Classic time series example `economics` data from `{ggplot2}` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} economics ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 574 × 6 date pce pop psavert uempmed unemploy 1 1967-07-01 507. 198712 12.6 4.5 2944 2 1967-08-01 510. 198911 12.6 4.7 2945 3 1967-09-01 516. 199113 11.9 4.6 2958 4 1967-10-01 512. 199311 12.9 4.9 3143 5 1967-11-01 517. 199498 12.8 4.7 3066 6 1967-12-01 525. 199657 11.8 4.8 3018 7 1968-01-01 531. 199808 11.7 5.1 2878 8 1968-02-01 534. 199920 12.3 4.5 3001 9 1968-03-01 544. 200056 11.7 4.1 2877 10 1968-04-01 544 200208 12.3 4.6 2709 # ℹ 564 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Let's try it How do you think we'd fit a line plot to these data, showing unemployment ("_unemploy_") over time? . . . ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Layers What happens when we layer `geom_line()` and `geom_point()`? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + geom_point() ``` ::: [try it!]{style="color:#D55E00;"} . . . Not the best instance of this It would work better on a plot with fewer time points, but you get the idea # Labels `labs()` ## Axis Labels ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|6|7"} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Date", y = "Unemployment" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Title ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|8"} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Date", y = "Unemployment", title = "Unemployment Over Time" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Subtitle ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|9"} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Date", y = "Unemployment", title = "Unemployment Over Time", subtitle = "This is the subtitle" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Caption ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|10"} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Date", y = "Unemployment", title = "Unemployment Over Time", subtitle = "This is the subtitle", caption = "Created by Joe Nese" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Tag ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|11"} economics |> ggplot(aes(date, unemploy)) + geom_line() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Date", y = "Unemployment", title = "Unemployment Over Time", subtitle = "This is the subtitle", caption = "Created by Joe Nese", tag = "(A)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Legend (one way) ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|2,8"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g, color = species)) + # 'color = ' geom_point() + theme_minimal() + labs( x = "Bill Length (mm)", y = "Body Mass (g)", color = "Species!" # 'color = ' ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/axes-6-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Facets ## Faceting * One of the most powerful features of `{ggplot2}` * Produce *n* plots by a specific variable * `facet_wrap()` + wrap a sequence of panels into two dimensions + based on variables(s) ## Faceting ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|5"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(~species) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/facet-1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Careful about the `~` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(species) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! object 'species' not found ``` ::: ::: ## Faceting two variables (like a matrix) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|5"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(species ~ year) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Alternative specification - `vars()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|5"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(vars(species)) ``` :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|5"} penguins |> ggplot(aes(bill_length_mm, body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(vars(species, year)) ``` ::: # Heatmaps > A heatmap is a literal way of visualizing a table of numbers, where you substitute the numbers with colored cells.
- Nathan Yau * Useful for finding highs and lows - and sometimes patterns * They don't always work well ## Example with correlations ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} corr <- cor(mtcars) pc <- corr |> as.data.frame() |> tibble::rownames_to_column("row") |> pivot_longer( cols = -row, names_to = "col", values_to = "cor" ) head(pc) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 3 row col cor 1 mpg mpg 1 2 mpg cyl -0.852 3 mpg disp -0.848 4 mpg hp -0.776 5 mpg drat 0.681 6 mpg wt -0.868 ``` ::: ::: ## Heatmap ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pc |> ggplot(aes(row, col, fill = cor)) + geom_tile() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-27-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Viridis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="|4"} pc |> ggplot(aes(row, col, fill = cor)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-28-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # Distributions ## Plotting Distributions - Histograms - Frequency Polygons - Density - Boxplots - Violin ## Data `ggplot2::diamonds` ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 53,940 × 10 carat cut color clarity depth table price x y z 1 0.23 Ideal E SI2 61.5 55 326 3.95 3.98 2.43 2 0.21 Premium E SI1 59.8 61 326 3.89 3.84 2.31 3 0.23 Good E VS1 56.9 65 327 4.05 4.07 2.31 4 0.29 Premium I VS2 62.4 58 334 4.2 4.23 2.63 5 0.31 Good J SI2 63.3 58 335 4.34 4.35 2.75 6 0.24 Very Good J VVS2 62.8 57 336 3.94 3.96 2.48 7 0.24 Very Good I VVS1 62.3 57 336 3.95 3.98 2.47 8 0.26 Very Good H SI1 61.9 55 337 4.07 4.11 2.53 9 0.22 Fair E VS2 65.1 61 337 3.87 3.78 2.49 10 0.23 Very Good H VS1 59.4 61 338 4 4.05 2.39 # ℹ 53,930 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Histogram Histogram of "price" ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-31-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Transparency - `alpha` Add some transparency – perhaps this looks nicer ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="3"} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-32-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## `color` vs. `fill` **In general** * `color` defines the color a geom is *outlined* * `fill` defines the color a geom is *filled* ## `color` vs. `fill` For example: * `geom_point()` default has only has a color and **NO** fill because they're just points * Point shapes 21–24 include both a color and a fill ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-33-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## How would we change the color of this plot? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7) ``` ::: ## How would we change the color of this plot? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7, color = "magenta") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-35-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## How would we change the ~~color~~ fill of this plot? ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(alpha = 0.7, fill = "magenta") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-36-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Color by variable What if we wanted different colors by a variable -- *species* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(aes(fill = cut), alpha = 0.7) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-37-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## `geom_freqpoly()` {.smaller} - `geom_histogram()` + histograms display the count with bars - `geom_freqpoly()` + frequency polygons display the counts with lines . . . :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} `geom_histogram` - note `fill = cut` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_histogram(aes(fill = cut), alpha = 0.7) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-38-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} `geom_freqpoly` - note `color = cut` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = price)) + geom_freqpoly(aes(color = cut), alpha = 0.7) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-39-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Density plot Alternative representation of distribution * Think of it as a smoothed histogram (uses kernel smoothing) + BUT, density is on the *y*-axis and **NOT** count * The depiction of the distribution is **NOT** determined by the number of the bins you use, as are histograms ## Density plot `geom_density()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g)) + geom_density() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-40-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Density plot Now let’s fill by *species* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g)) + geom_density(aes(fill = species), alpha = 0.2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-41-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Possible alternative? `facet_wrap` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = body_mass_g)) + geom_density(alpha = 0.2) + facet_wrap(~species) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-42-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Bar/Col Charts {.smaller} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **`geom_bar()`** * if you want to count the number of cases at each *x* or *y* position * expects *x* **OR** *y* * counts rows * makes the height of the bar proportional to the number of cases in each group * uses `stat_count()` by default ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **`geom_col()`** * if you want the heights of the bars to represent values in the data * expects *x* **AND** *y* * expects numbers in your data * leaves the data as is

* uses `stat_identity()` by default ::: :::: ## `geom_bar()` *mpg* data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mpg |> ggplot(aes(class)) + # one variable in the `aes()` geom_bar() # counts the rows per class ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-53-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## *summarized_mpg* data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summarized_mpg <- mpg |> group_by(class) |> count() head(summarized_mpg) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 2 # Groups: class [6] class n 1 2seater 5 2 compact 47 3 midsize 41 4 minivan 11 5 pickup 33 6 subcompact 35 ``` ::: ::: ## `geom_col()` *summarized_mpg* data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summarized_mpg |> ggplot(aes(class, n)) + # two variables in the `aes()` geom_col() # data has the rows per class in "n" ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-55-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} `geom_bar()` default ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mpg |> ggplot(aes(class)) + geom_bar() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-56-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%" .fragment} `geom_bar(stat = "identity")` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summarized_mpg |> ggplot(aes(class, n)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](w3_ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-57-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Let's talk themes * The default is `theme_gray()` + I don't like it * But there are a lot of build-in alternative in `{ggplot2}` + `theme_minimal()` is my favorite * Check out the [`{ggthemes}`](https://yutannihilation.github.io/allYourFigureAreBelongToUs/ggthemes/) package for a lot of alternatives + These days I often use the [`colorblind`](https://yutannihilation.github.io/allYourFigureAreBelongToUs/ggthemes/colorblind/) theme for discrete values in my plots + I also like the [`{MetBrewer}`](https://github.com/BlakeRMills/MetBrewer) package, inspired by art in the Met * Check out the [`{ggthemeassist}`](https://github.com/calligross/ggthemeassist) add-in # More themes * The [`{hrbrthemes}`](https://github.com/hrbrmstr/hrbrthemes) are nice * Consider [building your own theme!](https://bookdown.org/rdpeng/RProgDA/building-a-new-theme.html) * Or Google around . . . * Set the theme globally + One of the first lines in your .qmd file (after you load packages) could be: `theme_set(theme_minimal())` ## Resources The `{ggplot2}` package is one of the most popular `R` packages, and there are many resources to learn the syntax * ggplot2 book (email me for digital copy) * Posit [cheat sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-visualization.html) very helpful + Perhaps moreso after a little experience * [R Graphics Cookbook](http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/) * [R Graph Gallery](https://www.r-graph-gallery.com/index.html) + past students have really liked this one ##
